text:
William Carrier has two Stanley Cup rings, one from Vegas and one from last spring in Carolina, and a reputation built on hits (74 already this season). Yahoo Sports says he's thriving in an unexpected role, and the numbers agree, mostly.

The Hurricanes take about 63% of expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, a remarkable figure for a forward playing 13 minutes a night with no power-play time. He has 13 assists, already close to last season's 11. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 97th percentile of forwards for taking chances away last season, though with strong teammates.

The one thing missing is goals. He has one, on 5.5 expected, a 2.6% shooting rate from a player who normally shoots around 11%. That is about as clear a case of bad luck as there is in the league right now, and goals tend to follow chances. What to watch: the first few going in, and whether Carolina rewards a fourth-line role this productive with more ice time.
headline: Carrier keeps getting the looks
